Replicate the response from the posterior

Source: R/posterior_predictive.R
posterior_predictive.Rd

Draws replicate datasets from the fitted model, one per posterior draw, so that the data can be compared with what the model says they should look like. This is the individual-level check that fit_loo is not: LOO compares model structures by held-out predictive density, while this shows which features of the data the fit reproduces.

Usage

posterior_predictive(fit, ndraws = 100, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'stanimal_yrep'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'stanimal_yrep'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fit from lmm_animal or lm_phen_cov.

ndraws

Number of posterior draws to replicate from; taken evenly across the kept draws, so both warmup-free chains are represented.

seed

Optional seed for the simulation, to make the replicates reproducible. The sampler's seed does not cover this step.

...

Unused; for method compatibility.

x

An object returned by posterior_predictive().

Value

An object of class stanimal_yrep: a list with yrep (individuals by traits by draws, the same layout as fit_draws, with draws last), the observed y on the original response scale, the trait names, and the number of replicates. print() reports, for the trait means, standard deviations and pairwise correlations, the observed value, the 95% interval of the replicates, and p: the share of replicates at or above the observed value, a posterior predictive tail probability. These probabilities are not generally uniform under a correct model because the data are used both to fit and to check it. Values near 0 or 1 can flag a discrepancy; a middling value does not establish a good fit. plot() shows the replicate distributions.

Details

For an animal fit the replicate is \(X\beta + u + e\) with \(u \sim N(0, A \otimes G)\) and \(e \sim N(0, I \otimes E)\); for a phenotypic fit it is \(X\beta + e\) with \(e \sim N(0, P)\). G, E and P are the reported draws, so they are already on the response scale.

Replicates are simulated for every trait of every individual, including the entries that were not observed, so y is the response as it was passed in and has NA where the data are incomplete. Printed and plotted summaries compare each replicate on the same observed entries as the corresponding statistic in y. Pairs with fewer than two jointly observed values or constant observed values are omitted with a warning.

See also

fit_loo

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pp <- posterior_predictive(fit)
pp                      # observed against replicated summaries
plot(pp)                # and the distributions behind them
} # }
